title: Pardons Steven Samuel Grantham
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Steven Samuel Grantham as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s list records that Trump pardoned Steven Samuel Grantham on January 19, 2021. It identifies a 1967 Central District of California conviction for interstate transportation of a stolen vehicle and a sentence of four months in prison followed by two years of supervised release. The official entry confirms the pardon but does not explain the case or the decision.
description_long: The Justice Department’s official clemency list records Steven Samuel Grantham among the people President Donald Trump pardoned on January 19, 2021. It identifies a Central District of California conviction dated June 13, 1967, for interstate transportation of a stolen vehicle. The sentence listed was four months’ imprisonment followed by two years of supervised release. The dates place the pardon more than five decades after the sentence. DOJ’s table gives a concise case record, but it does not describe the vehicle or conduct involved, state whether Grantham served the full sentence, or explain why the administration granted clemency. The account can therefore report the offense, sentence, and pardon date without implying a particular motive or political relationship. The entry confirms that a pardon was issued; a fuller narrative of the case or decision would require the underlying clemency papers or case records, which the summary listing does not reproduce.

title: Pardons Gregory Louis Reyes
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Gregory Louis Reyes as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department lists Gregory Louis Reyes as pardoned by Trump on January 19, 2021. Its record identifies a 2010 Northern District of California sentence of 18 months in prison, two years of supervised release, and a $15 million fine for securities- and mail-fraud offenses involving Brocade stock and false SEC filings. The list confirms the grant but gives no rationale.
description_long: The Justice Department’s official clemency list records Gregory Louis Reyes among the people President Donald Trump pardoned on January 19, 2021. The table identifies a Northern District of California sentence dated June 24, 2010: 18 months’ imprisonment, two years of supervised release, and a $15 million fine. It lists conspiracy to commit securities and mail fraud, fraud involving Brocade stock, false SEC filings, falsified books and records, and false statements to an accountant. These are the offenses in DOJ’s summary; the page does not recount the evidence or underlying transactions. It also does not explain why Trump granted the pardon or state the administration’s decision process. The official list supports a description of the pardon and the case’s listed offenses and sentence, but it does not establish a connection between the clemency and any political contribution or relationship. A detailed account of the conviction or the pardon decision would require the underlying court and clemency records.

title: Commutes Sentence of James Brian Cruz
description_short: Trump commuted the sentence of James Brian Cruz as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department records that Trump commuted James Brian Cruz’s sentence on January 19, 2021. Its list identifies a 2001 Western District of Texas conviction for conspiracy to possess more than 500 grams of methamphetamine with intent to distribute, with a sentence of 480 months, five years of supervised release, and a $25,000 fine. The listing does not state the new terms.
description_long: The Justice Department’s official list records James Brian Cruz among the people whose sentences President Donald Trump commuted on January 19, 2021. It identifies a Western District of Texas conviction dated June 26, 2001, for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute more than 500 grams of methamphetamine. The sentence listed was 480 months’ imprisonment, five years of supervised release, and a $25,000 fine. That is the original sentence recorded in the clemency list; the summary does not say how much of it the commutation removed, whether Cruz was released, or what supervision conditions remained afterward. The action was a commutation, not a pardon, so the conviction itself is not described as erased. The exact clemency terms are necessary to explain the practical result. Until the warrant or an updated sentence record is available, the account can confirm the offense and original sentence but not the relief Cruz actually received.

title: DTTM Operations applies to trademark TRUMP TV after White House channel launch
description_short: DTTM Operations applies to trademark TRUMP TV after White House channel launch
description_medium: Trademark attorney Josh Gerben reported that DTTM Operations filed a TRUMP TV application on September 24, after the White House launched a stream using that name. Newsweek also reported the filing. The application concerns a private Trump entity; it does not establish a granted trademark or a government licensing payment.
description_long: Trademark attorney Josh Gerben reported that DTTM Operations filed an application for the TRUMP TV mark on September 24, 2026, at 11:20 a.m. Eastern. The filing came three days after the White House launched a stream using the same name. Newsweek described the application as covering television, streaming, and software products or services. DTTM Operations is a private Trump entity, so the application records a company’s request to register a mark; it does not show that the U.S. government licensed the name or paid the company. The filing also is not a granted trademark. It marks an early step in the registration process, and the supplied material does not establish an outcome from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, a licensing arrangement, or any government payment. The event is the timing and overlap between a White House-branded stream and a private company’s application. Those facts alone do not establish that the stream used the mark under a paid or exclusive arrangement.
